question:
**Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.**

Holding on to something or keeping an opinion with determination
solution:
The correct answer is **"Tenacious".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **One word replacement** is the use of **one word **in place of a **long phrase to simplify the sentence structure**.
 
• If someone describes you as **tenacious**, they presumably mean that **you never give up and never stop trying. **(दृढ़)
 
 
• **Example - **The baby took my finger in its **tenacious **little fist. ​
 
 
 
• Therefore,** option 2)** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The meanings of the given other options are below:
 
 
• **Gracious:** Being **gracious** is being **considerate and kind. **(विनीत)
 
• **Obnoxious:** **Obnoxious** behavior is described as **being very unpleasant, offensive, or repulsive. **(अप्रिय)
 
• **Loquacious:** A **loquacious** person is a person who speaks a lot. (बातूनी)
